raw.title: DevOps Team Manager
raw.description:
Bromcom Computers Plc is the UK's fastest-growing cloud-native school Management Information System (MIS) provider, serving thousands of schools across three UK countries. The DevOps Team Manager leads a team of 3-4 engineers and is accountable for the reliable, secure and controlled operation of Bromcom's Azure-first SaaS platform. This is a hands-on DevOps engineering leadership role with an expected balance of 70% hands-on DevOps engineering and 30% people and team management. The manager works closely with the engineers, contributes directly to delivery and operations, and owns completion and ongoing maintenance of the agreed DevOps operational control improvements.

The role requires a credible engineering background. The successful candidate is expected to work directly across Azure platform engineering, CI/CD, Bicep/ARM, automation, incident response and operational controls, while leading the team and setting standards. They must be able to challenge technical decisions, understand operational risk and failure modes, and ensure agreed processes are implemented, followed, evidenced and continually improved. A control is not complete simply because a policy or tool exists; it must work consistently in practice.

Key Responsibilities

People & Team Leadership

  • Lead, line-manage and develop a team of 3-4 DevOps engineers, including at least one senior engineer; own recruitment, onboarding, objectives, appraisals and performance management.

  • Set clear role boundaries, decision rights and escalation routes; ensure high-risk activities are performed or approved only by people with the required competence and authority.

  • Own team capacity, priorities and the out-of-hours on-call rota. The manager is expected to take a fair share of scheduled rota cover alongside the engineers and respond to production incidents and urgent operational issues during that cover, including evenings, weekends and bank holidays where required. Ensure rota coverage, handovers, escalation routes and recovery time are planned and sustainable, while protecting time for reliability, control improvement, technical debt, training and documentation.

  • Build an accountable coaching culture in which engineers raise risk early, follow agreed standards, maintain evidence and learn from incidents and control failures.

Engineering & Platform Leadership

  • Provide hands-on engineering leadership for Bromcom's Azure-hosted, multi-tenant SaaS platform. Work closely with engineers to design, build, review, troubleshoot and improve platform services, pipelines, Infrastructure-as-Code, automation and operational tooling. The manager remains accountable for technical quality while enabling engineers to own their work.

  • Set and maintain engineering standards for Azure architecture, Azure DevOps, Bicep/ARM, deployment patterns, observability, resilience, security and operational support.

  • Challenge designs and changes using risk, maintainability, failure-mode, rollback and supportability thinking; involve senior engineers and technical leadership where specialist authority is required.

  • Own platform SLAs/SLOs, service health, major-incident command, root-cause analysis, disaster recovery, business continuity testing and continuous service improvement.

Operational Controls, Standards & Compliance

  • Take day-to-day ownership within the DevOps team for implementing the agreed operational control improvement plan, driving actions to completion and then maintaining the controls as part of normal team operation.

  • Implement and enforce an end-to-end change lifecycle covering request, design, risk assessment, peer or senior review, testing, approval, implementation, post-change verification and formal closure.

  • Ensure policies, standard operating procedures, runbooks, RACI and ownership arrangements, approval thresholds and evidence requirements remain current, practical and aligned across Azure DevOps, SysAid and other operational systems.

  • Ensure production and customer-impacting changes, including emergency changes and customer-specific change notices, have proportionate risk classification, segregation of duties, pre-production evidence, approval, rollback plans and traceable outcomes.

  • Maintain audit-ready evidence for changes, deployments, access, incidents, disaster-recovery tests, vulnerabilities, exceptions and corrective actions, aligned with Bromcom's security, quality, service-management, UK GDPR and customer obligations.

  • Confirm controls are operating effectively, not simply documented or configured. Track exceptions, overdue actions and repeat failures to closure, with clear corrective actions and independent assurance where required.

  • Provide weekly control reporting and escalate material risk, blocked actions or insufficient capacity promptly. Work with QA, Compliance, Security and technical leads to translate procedural controls into automated technical gates where practical.

Delivery, Automation & AI

  • Work directly with engineers to design, build, review and continually improve Azure DevOps CI/CD pipelines and Bicep/ARM Infrastructure-as-Code, including automated approvals, testing, security checks, evidence capture and post-deployment verification.

  • Reduce manual toil and unsafe variation through automation, reusable platform patterns and clear service ownership; ensure manual exceptions are visible, justified, time-bound and reviewed.

  • Set the strategy and guardrails for AI-assisted and agentic DevOps delivery across CI/CD, Infrastructure-as-Code generation, incident triage, log analysis, runbook automation and documentation.

  • Use and govern AI engineering tools such as Claude, GitHub Copilot or Codex, with clear quality, security, data-protection and human accountability controls. Apply them practically to increase delivery speed, quality and reliability, while ensuring an engineer remains accountable for every output and change.

Security, Identity & FinOps

  • Own platform identity, privileged-access and secrets-management controls, including Entra ID, Key Vault, OAuth, certificate automation, WAF and network security across VNets, App Gateway, S2S VPN and DNS.

  • Ensure access follows least-privilege principles, is reviewed regularly and is supported by effective joiner-mover-leaver, break-glass and segregation-of-duties controls.

  • Own observability standards across Azure Monitor and Grafana, security and vulnerability follow-up, and cloud cost and FinOps accountability for the Azure estate.

Stakeholder & Cross-Team Influence

  • Act as the accountable management and technical escalation point across Software Engineering, CloudOps, IT and Security, QA and Compliance, and external partners, working with senior engineers on design-authority decisions.

  • Provide concise, conclusions-first reporting to the CTO and Executive Team on service health, delivery, control effectiveness, risks, exceptions and improvement progress.

  • Contribute to Bromcom's software delivery transformation programme and align the DevOps operating model and controls with AIDP and wider software-engineering standards.

Person Specification

Essential

  • Proven line-management experience leading a DevOps, CloudOps or platform team, with accountability for recruitment, objectives, appraisals, development and performance management.

  • Current hands-on experience in DevOps, cloud or platform engineering, with the ability to contribute directly to architecture, Azure platform work, pipelines, Bicep/ARM Infrastructure-as-Code, automation, troubleshooting, security and resilience. Candidates should expect approximately 70% of the role to involve hands-on engineering delivery.

  • Evidence of implementing and maintaining operational controls, processes and procedures in a DevOps or CloudOps environment, including ownership of improvement actions, exceptions, corrective actions and audit evidence.

  • Practical command of end-to-end change and release governance, including risk classification, peer or senior review, testing, approvals, segregation of duties, rollback, emergency change, post-change verification and closure.

  • Deep Azure platform expertise across Entra ID, App Services, Key Vault, App Gateway, VNets, Azure SQL or MySQL, WAF and DNS.

  • Strong CI/CD and Infrastructure-as-Code knowledge across Azure DevOps pipelines and Bicep/ARM for Windows and Linux workloads, with the ability to govern standards and technical gates.

  • A track record of operating production, multi-tenant SaaS at scale, including SLA/SLO ownership, major-incident command, root-cause analysis, disaster recovery and service improvement. Willingness and ability to participate personally in the out-of-hours on-call rota, including scheduled evening, weekend and bank-holiday cover where required.

  • Experience working with security, compliance and audit teams in a regulated or data-sensitive environment, with the ability to turn policies into workable controls and demonstrate that they operate effectively.

  • Demonstrable practical use of Claude, GitHub Copilot or Codex as engineering delivery tools, with sound governance, secure use and accountable human review.

  • Clear senior-level communication and reporting, with the discipline to assign owners, manage risks and dependencies, challenge weak evidence and pursue actions through to verified closure.

Desirable

  • Experience leading an operational-control improvement or remediation programme in an ISO 27001 or similarly controlled environment.

  • Containerisation and orchestration experience across AKS or Kubernetes and Docker for multi-tenant workloads.

  • Knowledge of ITIL or service-management controls and practical use of service desk or work-management platforms such as SysAid.

  • Experience in education, public sector, health, finance or another data-sensitive sector, including familiarity with UK GDPR and customer-specific change controls.

  • Relevant certification, such as Azure Solutions Architect Expert or DevOps Engineer Expert.

Our partner is looking for an AI Research Engineer (Kernel & Inference Optimization) based in United Kingdom. You will work at the intersection of AI research, systems engineering, and high-performance model inference. Your focus will be on developing and optimizing model-serving architectures for advanced AI systems across a range of hardware environments. You will tackle challenges involving latency, throughput, memory efficiency, and scalability, including deployment on resource-constrained mobile and edge devices. The role combines hands-on research with low-level engineering, giving you the opportunity to develop novel inference strategies and GPU kernels. You will work with complex architectures spanning text, image, audio, diffusion models, and vision transformers. Your work will involve rigorous benchmarking, production testing, and iterative optimization to translate research into measurable performance improvements. You will collaborate with cross-functional teams in a highly technical, remote environment focused on pushing the boundaries of efficient AI systems. Accountabilities Design and deploy advanced model-serving architectures optimized for high throughput, low latency, and efficient memory utilization. Develop inference pipelines capable of operating effectively across diverse environments, including resource-constrained mobile devices and edge platforms. Establish clear performance targets covering response latency, token generation speed, throughput, memory footprint, and reliability. Build and execute controlled inference benchmarks in simulated and production environments, tracking latency, throughput, memory consumption, and error rates. Create and maintain representative datasets and simulation scenarios for evaluating model performance under real-world and resource-constrained conditions. Identify computational and memory bottlenecks across inference pipelines and implement solutions involving batching, networking, memory management, and other system-level optimizations. Develop custom GPU kernels and compute shaders for mobile hardware, including solutions written in Metal Shading Language (MSL). Apply advanced inference optimization techniques such as pruning, quantization, Flash Attention, KV caching, and speculative decoding. Design and optimize distributed inference systems using approaches such as tensor parallelism, pipeline parallelism, and expert parallelism for large-scale GPU workloads. Work with cross-functional engineering and research teams to integrate optimized inference frameworks into production and edge-device applications. Define evaluation methodologies, document experimental results, compare performance against established benchmarks, and continuously refine optimization strategies. Monitor production performance and use empirical research to identify opportunities for further improvements in scalability, efficiency, and reliability. Requirements: Degree in Computer Science or a related technical field; a PhD in NLP, Machine Learning, or a related discipline is highly relevant, particularly with a strong AI research track record and publications at leading conferences. Proven expertise in Metal Shading Language (MSL), including the ability to write custom compute shaders from scratch. Demonstrated experience with low-level kernel optimization and inference optimization on mobile or other resource-constrained devices. Track record of delivering measurable improvements in inference latency, throughput, and memory footprint for domain-specific applications. Deep understanding of modern model-serving architectures, inference engines, and optimization techniques for high-performance AI deployment. Strong experience writing GPU kernels for mobile devices such as smartphones. Practical experience developing and deploying end-to-end inference pipelines, from model optimization through production integration on constrained hardware. Strong ability to apply empirical research and systematic experimentation to solve latency, computational, and memory challenges. Experience designing robust evaluation and benchmarking frameworks for inference systems. Knowledge of distributed inference techniques, including tensor parallelism, pipeline parallelism, and expert parallelism for large-scale GPU clusters. Deep understanding of the mathematical foundations and architecture of diffusion models and Vision Transformers. Familiarity with modern inference optimization techniques including pruning, quantization, Flash Attention, KV Cache optimization, and speculative decoding such as EAGLE. Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, with an ability to investigate complex system bottlenecks and turn research findings into practical engineering solutions. Excellent English communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively with distributed, cross-functional technical teams. Benefits: Opportunity to work on advanced AI systems spanning model serving, inference optimization, mobile computing, edge deployment, and large-scale distributed inference. Remote-first working environment with an international team. Exposure to cutting-edge AI research and practical systems engineering challenges. Opportunity to contribute to performance-critical infrastructure where improvements can have a measurable impact on real-world AI applications. Collaborative environment combining research-driven experimentation with hands-on engineering. Opportunity to work with advanced model architectures including diffusion models, Vision Transformers, and multimodal systems. Access to challenging technical problems involving GPU kernels, inference engines, memory optimization, and distributed computing. At Mews, we’re transforming the industry with a platform that helps hotels run smarter, move faster and create better guest experiences.</p> <p>You’ll work with smart, curious people who care deeply about what they do. You’ll have autonomy and the trust to make good decisions and move quickly. And you’ll enjoy a real sense of purpose as you see the impact of what we’re building.</p> <p>If you’re motivated by ownership, curiosity and meaningful impact, and are driven to deliver consistent high performance, you’ll feel at home here.</p> <h4><strong>About the role</strong></h4> <p>Let's get into the specifics. It’s impossible to capture every nuance of a role – especially at a rapidly growing company like Mews – but if we had to distil it into a job description (which we do because this is a job description), it would be this:</p></div><p>You'd own the design and delivery of Mews' first dedicated commercial enablement function inside Onboarding: turning onboarding professionals across a global, distributed team into consultants who can spot and act on expansion revenue, without inheriting anyone else's playbook.</p> <p>Most onboarding organisations treat go-live as the finish line, so the upsell and cross-sell signals sitting inside existing project portfolios go unqualified and never reach Sales. At Mews, that gap sits inside a fast-growing hospitality tech customer base, where every project portfolio onboarding already manages is effectively an unworked pipeline of expansion revenue.</p> <p>You'll work closely with Onboarding leadership globally, plus Sales, Customer Success and RevOps, to define what a qualified expansion lead looks like and get it moving to the right team. This is a new role, not a backfill, so the coaching model, playbooks and success metrics are yours to build from scratch.</p> <p>This role exists because Onboarding's project portfolios are growing faster than the team's ability to work them commercially, and right now, nobody owns that motion end to end.</p> <h4><strong>What you would do</strong></h4> <ul> <li>Design and deliver consultative sales training for onboarding professionals, covering discovery, opportunity qualification, objection handling and commercial conversations that keep the customer's trust intact</li> <li>Build an ongoing coaching programme that grows consultative skill progressively, from new joiners through tenured consultants, and onboard new starters into the commercial side of the role from day one</li> <li>Develop playbooks and frameworks, including AI-assisted tools, that help the team surface and qualify upsell and cross-sell signals across their project portfolios at scale</li> <li>Partner with Sales, Customer Success and RevOps to define a qualified expansion lead and build the handoff process between Onboarding and Sales</li> <li>Track commercial performance across the portfolio (pipeline generated, expansion revenue influenced, handoff quality) and use it to keep improving the programme</li> </ul> <p><strong>AI Fluency Level 3:</strong> in this role, that means redesigning how the wider onboarding team spots and qualifies commercial signals, not just using AI to work faster yourself. You'll build AI-assisted frameworks and tools that other onboarding professionals can use on their own portfolios, and you'll actively check what those tools flag before it shapes a playbook or gets treated as a qualified lead.</p> <p><em>For more information on AI fluency at Mews, please refer to <a href="https://mews.atlassian.net/wiki/x/XQOskg">"AI Fluency at Mews: A Comprehensive Guide for Candidates"</a>.</em></p> <h4><strong>What you would bring</strong>&nbsp;</h4> <ul> <li>4+ years in Revenue Enablement, Sales Enablement or Commercial Training, with direct exposure to consultative or solution-selling methodologies</li> <li>A background as a quota-carrying sales rep, account manager or customer success leader: you've had the commercial conversations you'll be teaching others to We’re motivated to proactively use the technology to seek out better ways of working and share our findings with the rest of the company.</li> </ul> <p>If there's anything we can do to support you during the application process, let us know.</p> <p>We don't discriminate on the basis of race, religion, colour, nationality, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other protected characteristic.</p> <p>One final thing: don't hold back. description: <div> <div class="attachment-overlay preview"> <div id="viewer-container"> <div id="canvas-container"> <div id="viewer" class="pdfViewer"></div> </div> </div> </div> </div> <p><strong>About Tripadvisor</strong></p> <p>The Tripadvisor Group connects people to experiences worth sharing, and aims to be the world’s most trusted source for travel and experiences. We leverage our brands, technology, and capabilities to connect our global audience with partners through rich content, travel guidance, and two-sided marketplaces for experiences, accommodations, restaurants, and other travel categories. The subsidiaries of Tripadvisor, Inc. (Nasdaq: TRIP), include a portfolio of travel brands and businesses, including Tripadvisor, Viator, and TheFork.</p> <p><strong>Tripadvisor Experiences Engineering</strong> is the team that builds and supports the <strong>world's leading marketplace for travel experiences</strong>. We believe that making memories is what travel is all about. And with 400,000+ travel experiences to explore—everything from simple tours to extreme adventures (and everything in between) —making memories that will last a lifetime has never been easier.</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>About the Role</strong></p> <p>We’re looking for a curious, high-potential<strong> Software Engineer I</strong> to join our Experiences Engineering team. This is a junior,<strong> full-stack</strong> role, working with <strong>Java, SQL, React, AWS and AI tools</strong>. It’s designed for engineers who have strong fundamentals and are hungry to grow in a fast-paced, product-driven environment. If you love the idea of shipping code to millions of travelers and want to learn how to build at scale, this is the place for you!</p> <p>We embrace flexibility in where and how work gets done and also value meaningful in-person moments to connect and collaborate. You can expect a<strong> remote-first working model</strong> with periodic in-person gatherings at your closest office for team connection, planning, or other key moments. This position is open to candidates based within a commutable distance (generally up to 1 hour) of one of our office hubs in&nbsp;<strong>London, Oxford, Krakow or Lisbon.</strong></p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>What You’ll Do&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Ship Frequently: </strong>You’ll be part of the full software lifecycle, from design and coding to testing and deployment. You’ll release code to production on an almost daily basis.</li> <li><strong>Learn &amp; Grow: </strong>Work cross-functionally alongside product, design, and data experts to understand why we build, not just how.</li> <li><strong>Partner with AI:</strong> Leverage agentic coding tools for routine tasks like writing boilerplate, unit tests, and small refactors, using AI as a "force multiplier" to help you learn faster.</li> <li><strong>Build Quality: </strong>Design and implement clean, readable solutions with a strong focus on automated unit and integration testing.</li> <li><strong>Collaborate: </strong>Participate in design reviews, ask questions, and actively seek feedback to sharpen your technical and professional skills.</li> </ul> <p><br><br></p> <p><strong>Skills &amp; Experience&nbsp;</strong></p> <p>We typically look for 0-2 years’ experience, following a Bachelor’s degree or above in Comp Sci.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Technical Fundamentals</strong>: A strong grasp of computer science basics—data structures, algorithms, and object-oriented programming.</li> <li><strong>Full-Stack Exposure:</strong> Familiarity with web app development, including proficiency in at least one modern backend language (e.g., Java, C#, Go, Python) and a basic understanding of relational databases like MySQL or PostgreSQL.</li> <li><strong>AI Coding:</strong> you are comfortable coding with either Cursor or Codex/Claude/Open Code.&nbsp;</li> <li><strong>Growth Mindset</strong>: A genuine desire to learn new technologies and a "global-first" mindset for collaborating with teammates around the world.</li> <li><strong>Clear Communication: </strong>The ability to explain your logic and talk through blockers with your team.</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p>We don’t expect you to know everything on day one. However, we’re especially interested if you’ve had exposure to AWS, React, or NoSQL databases. More than any specific tool, we value curiosity and the ability to solve problems creatively.&nbsp;</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p>We value engineers from different technical backgrounds. You can complete our<strong> coding interview exercises</strong> in any language of your choice, but need to be open to working within the Java ecosystem when you join!</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>What We Offer</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Competitive compensation packages</strong>, including base salary, annual bonus, and more.</li> <li><strong>“Work your way”</strong> with flexibility to suit your lifestyle. We take a remote-friendly approach to collaboration, with the option to join on-site as often as you’d like in select locations.&nbsp;</li> <li><strong>Flexible schedule</strong>. Work-life balance is ingrained in our culture by design. Trust and accountability make it work.</li> <li><strong>Donation matching</strong>. Give back? Give more! We match qualifying charitable donations annually.</li> <li><strong>Tuition assistance</strong>. Want to level up your career? We love to hear it! Receive annual support for qualified programs.</li> <li><strong>Lifestyle benefit</strong>. An annual benefit to spend on yourself. Use it on travel, wellness, or whatever suits you.</li> <li><strong>Travel perks</strong>. We believe that travel is employee development, so we provide discounts and more.</li> <li><strong>Employee assistance program</strong>. We’re here for you with resources and programs to help you through life’s challenges.</li> <li><strong>Health benefits</strong>. We offer great coverage and competitive premiums.</li> <li><strong>Generous referral scheme.</strong> Help us grow and be rewarded with generous awards for referring successful candidates.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Our Cultural Pillars:</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Traveller first: </strong>We exist to create value for our customer, the traveler. We enable our suppliers and partners to unlock this value. Their collective behaviors and insights are what drives us.&nbsp;</li> <li><strong>Execution is our edge: </strong>We act fast, experiment, learn from failure, iterate, and improve the solutions of tomorrow across every aspect of our business. Our execution is agile, data-driven, prioritised, and built to scale. We assume no problem is someone else’s problem and finish what can be done today, knowing tomorrow will bring fresh challenges.&nbsp;</li> <li><strong>We succeed together: </strong>The best outcomes are driven by empathic, humble, and diverse subject matter experts working toward shared goals. We collaborate relentlessly, challenge assumptions, give actionable feedback, and set each other up for success through empowered teams with a clear charter. We transparently take ownership of our growth, individually and as a team. We celebrate the quality of our effort, our learnings, and our collective achievements.</li> </ul> <p>Discover more in our <a href="https://medium.com/tripadvisor">Tech Blog</a>, for an inside look into some of our exciting and ground-breaking technical projects here at Tripadvisor Group.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <p>Tripadvisor Group champions the unique identities, abilities, and experiences of all our people – employees, customers, and partners. This stems from our belief in the transformative power of travel, dining, and experiences to connect us and open doors to worlds very different from our own. title: AI Research Engineer (Kernel & Inference Optimization)
description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an AI Research Engineer (Kernel & Inference Optimization) based in France. You will work at the intersection of AI research, systems engineering, and high-performance model inference. Your focus will be on developing and optimizing model-serving architectures for advanced AI systems across a range of hardware environments. You will tackle challenges involving latency, throughput, memory efficiency, and scalability, including deployment on resource-constrained mobile and edge devices. The role combines hands-on research with low-level engineering, giving you the opportunity to develop novel inference strategies and GPU kernels. You will work with complex architectures spanning text, image, audio, diffusion models, and vision transformers. Your work will involve rigorous benchmarking, production testing, and iterative optimization to translate research into measurable performance improvements. You will collaborate with cross-functional teams in a highly technical, remote environment focused on pushing the boundaries of efficient AI systems. Accountabilities Design and deploy advanced model-serving architectures optimized for high throughput, low latency, and efficient memory utilization. Develop inference pipelines capable of operating effectively across diverse environments, including resource-constrained mobile devices and edge platforms. Establish clear performance targets covering response latency, token generation speed, throughput, memory footprint, and reliability. Build and execute controlled inference benchmarks in simulated and production environments, tracking latency, throughput, memory consumption, and error rates. Create and maintain representative datasets and simulation scenarios for evaluating model performance under real-world and resource-constrained conditions. Identify computational and memory bottlenecks across inference pipelines and implement solutions involving batching, networking, memory management, and other system-level optimizations. Develop custom GPU kernels and compute shaders for mobile hardware, including solutions written in Metal Shading Language (MSL). Apply advanced inference optimization techniques such as pruning, quantization, Flash Attention, KV caching, and speculative decoding. Design and optimize distributed inference systems using approaches such as tensor parallelism, pipeline parallelism, and expert parallelism for large-scale GPU workloads. Work with cross-functional engineering and research teams to integrate optimized inference frameworks into production and edge-device applications. Define evaluation methodologies, document experimental results, compare performance against established benchmarks, and continuously refine optimization strategies. Monitor production performance and use empirical research to identify opportunities for further improvements in scalability, efficiency, and reliability. Requirements: Degree in Computer Science or a related technical field; a PhD in NLP, Machine Learning, or a related discipline is highly relevant, particularly with a strong AI research track record and publications at leading conferences. Proven expertise in Metal Shading Language (MSL), including the ability to write custom compute shaders from scratch. Demonstrated experience with low-level kernel optimization and inference optimization on mobile or other resource-constrained devices. Track record of delivering measurable improvements in inference latency, throughput, and memory footprint for domain-specific applications. Deep understanding of modern model-serving architectures, inference engines, and optimization techniques for high-performance AI deployment. Strong experience writing GPU kernels for mobile devices such as smartphones. Practical experience developing and deploying end-to-end inference pipelines, from model optimization through production integration on constrained hardware. Strong ability to apply empirical research and systematic experimentation to solve latency, computational, and memory challenges. Experience designing robust evaluation and benchmarking frameworks for inference systems. Knowledge of distributed inference techniques, including tensor parallelism, pipeline parallelism, and expert parallelism for large-scale GPU clusters. Deep understanding of the mathematical foundations and architecture of diffusion models and Vision Transformers. Familiarity with modern inference optimization techniques including pruning, quantization, Flash Attention, KV Cache optimization, and speculative decoding such as EAGLE. Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, with an ability to investigate complex system bottlenecks and turn research findings into practical engineering solutions. Excellent English communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively with distributed, cross-functional technical teams. Benefits: Opportunity to work on advanced AI systems spanning model serving, inference optimization, mobile computing, edge deployment, and large-scale distributed inference. Remote-first working environment with an international team. Exposure to cutting-edge AI research and practical systems engineering challenges. Opportunity to contribute to performance-critical infrastructure where improvements can have a measurable impact on real-world AI applications. Collaborative environment combining research-driven experimentation with hands-on engineering. Opportunity to work with advanced model architectures including diffusion models, Vision Transformers, and multimodal systems. Access to challenging technical problems involving GPU kernels, inference engines, memory optimization, and distributed computing. Contribuez au service public de l'assainissement et à la qualité du traitement des eaux usées dans plus de 70 communes adhérentes sur le territoire de l’Amandinois, la Pévèle et le Douaisis en intégrant le Centre d’Exploitation de Pecquencourt Nord. Le territoire compte 15 stations d’épuration dans lesquelles nous utilisons le traitement biologique par boues activées, et 400 pompes de relèvement.

Au sein d’une équipe de 14 personnes et sous la supervision du Responsable d'équipe Assainissement, vous garantissez le bon fonctionnement et le dépannage des équipements électromécaniques assainissement du centre d'exploitation de Pecquencourt Nord, au service de communes adhérentes à notre compétence d'assainissement collectif.

En tant qu’électrotechnicien(ne), vous avez pour mission de :

  • Intervenir suite au signalement des dysfonctionnements électro-mécaniques remontés par notre système de supervision ;

  • Piloter et contrôler les performances des ouvrages d'assainissement collectif (stations d'épuration, de refoulement et réseaux) ;

  • Entretenir de façon préventive et curative les ouvrages ;

  • Intervenir sur le système de supervision.

Des astreintes sont prévues sur ce poste afin d'assurer la continuité du service public.

Ce que nous vous proposons :

  • Un temps de travail de 37,5 heures ;

  • 27 jours de congés payés ainsi que des RTT ;

  • Des frais de déplacements (paniers repas) ;

  • Une mutuelle d’entreprise de base ou option familiale.


Vous êtes… ?

  • Diplômé(e) d’un BTS Electrotechnique ou autre formation similaire et idéalement formé(e) au traitement de l’eau en assainissement ;

  • A l'aise dans les interventions mécaniques, électromécaniques et sur des installations de type industriel ;

  • Reconnu(e) comme une personne méthodique et réactive ;

  • Doté(e) d’un bon relationnel pour maintenir un esprit d’équipe constructif et solidaire ;

  • Capable de travailler seul(e) quotidiennement ;

  • Respectueux(-se) des règles de sécurité pour vous-même et votre entourage ;

  • Détenteur(-rice) du permis B (déplacements quotidiens sur les différents ouvrages).

title: Senior Business Analyst – Financial Crime Compliance & Market Conduct
description: <p>Joining Capco means becoming part of an innovative and dynamic consultancy firm, committed to fostering an inclusive environment where you are encouraged to #BeYourselfAtWork. We embrace individuality as a key factor in promoting diversity and inclusion, values that sit at the core of our success. We aim to attract a wide variety of talented professionals with different skills and experiences. If you require any adjustments to support your application process, please feel free to inform us at any stage.</p> <p><strong>ABOUT CAPCO</strong></p> <p>Capco is a global technology and business consultancy that is passionate about supporting clients in the financial services sector to grow and succeed in today's ever-changing world. We are:</p> <ul> <li>Experts in banking, capital markets, payments and asset and wealth management.</li> <li>Trusted advisors in core banking, securities and wealth management transformation, regulatory change, risk management and technology modernization.</li> <li>A company dedicated to continuous development and excited to welcome top talent to help us drive innovation and deliver lasting results.</li> <li>A business built on agility, collaboration, and entrepreneurial spirit.</li> </ul> <p><strong>THE ROLE</strong></p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p>We are looking for an experienced Senior Business Analyst to help shape the strategic transformation of our Financial Crime Compliance (FCC) and Market Conduct &amp; Trade Surveillance (MCTS) capabilities within Legal &amp; Compliance.</p> <p>Working at the intersection of compliance, business, technology, architecture and data, you will shape strategic target states, assess current capabilities and translate business and control objectives into prioritised transformation roadmaps and actionable requirements. description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an AI Research Engineer (Kernel & Inference Optimization) based in Switzerland. You will work at the intersection of AI research, systems engineering, and high-performance model inference. Your focus will be on developing and optimizing model-serving architectures for advanced AI systems across a range of hardware environments. You will tackle challenges involving latency, throughput, memory efficiency, and scalability, including deployment on resource-constrained mobile and edge devices. The role combines hands-on research with low-level engineering, giving you the opportunity to develop novel inference strategies and GPU kernels. You will work with complex architectures spanning text, image, audio, diffusion models, and vision transformers. Your work will involve rigorous benchmarking, production testing, and iterative optimization to translate research into measurable performance improvements. You will collaborate with cross-functional teams in a highly technical, remote environment focused on pushing the boundaries of efficient AI systems. Accountabilities Design and deploy advanced model-serving architectures optimized for high throughput, low latency, and efficient memory utilization. Develop inference pipelines capable of operating effectively across diverse environments, including resource-constrained mobile devices and edge platforms. Establish clear performance targets covering response latency, token generation speed, throughput, memory footprint, and reliability. Build and execute controlled inference benchmarks in simulated and production environments, tracking latency, throughput, memory consumption, and error rates. Create and maintain representative datasets and simulation scenarios for evaluating model performance under real-world and resource-constrained conditions. Identify computational and memory bottlenecks across inference pipelines and implement solutions involving batching, networking, memory management, and other system-level optimizations. Develop custom GPU kernels and compute shaders for mobile hardware, including solutions written in Metal Shading Language (MSL). Apply advanced inference optimization techniques such as pruning, quantization, Flash Attention, KV caching, and speculative decoding. Design and optimize distributed inference systems using approaches such as tensor parallelism, pipeline parallelism, and expert parallelism for large-scale GPU workloads. Work with cross-functional engineering and research teams to integrate optimized inference frameworks into production and edge-device applications. Define evaluation methodologies, document experimental results, compare performance against established benchmarks, and continuously refine optimization strategies. Monitor production performance and use empirical research to identify opportunities for further improvements in scalability, efficiency, and reliability. Requirements: Degree in Computer Science or a related technical field; a PhD in NLP, Machine Learning, or a related discipline is highly relevant, particularly with a strong AI research track record and publications at leading conferences. Proven expertise in Metal Shading Language (MSL), including the ability to write custom compute shaders from scratch. Demonstrated experience with low-level kernel optimization and inference optimization on mobile or other resource-constrained devices. Track record of delivering measurable improvements in inference latency, throughput, and memory footprint for domain-specific applications. Deep understanding of modern model-serving architectures, inference engines, and optimization techniques for high-performance AI deployment. Strong experience writing GPU kernels for mobile devices such as smartphones. Practical experience developing and deploying end-to-end inference pipelines, from model optimization through production integration on constrained hardware. Strong ability to apply empirical research and systematic experimentation to solve latency, computational, and memory challenges. Experience designing robust evaluation and benchmarking frameworks for inference systems. Knowledge of distributed inference techniques, including tensor parallelism, pipeline parallelism, and expert parallelism for large-scale GPU clusters. Deep understanding of the mathematical foundations and architecture of diffusion models and Vision Transformers. Familiarity with modern inference optimization techniques including pruning, quantization, Flash Attention, KV Cache optimization, and speculative decoding such as EAGLE. Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, with an ability to investigate complex system bottlenecks and turn research findings into practical engineering solutions. Excellent English communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively with distributed, cross-functional technical teams. Benefits: Opportunity to work on advanced AI systems spanning model serving, inference optimization, mobile computing, edge deployment, and large-scale distributed inference. Remote-first working environment with an international team. Exposure to cutting-edge AI research and practical systems engineering challenges. Opportunity to contribute to performance-critical infrastructure where improvements can have a measurable impact on real-world AI applications. Collaborative environment combining research-driven experimentation with hands-on engineering. Opportunity to work with advanced model architectures including diffusion models, Vision Transformers, and multimodal systems. Companies waste billions on bad ads, mismatched landing pages, and poor budget allocation. Uplane fixes this by building the AI technology for the marketing agency of the future. Our software supports creative producers with static ad creation, video ad creation, landing page design, and much more. We are building the AI software for the next generation of AI-native content producers and need ambitious, creative video producers with strong taste who will use our AI engine to deliver high-performing video ads for our customers.

About The Role

We're seeking a highly motivated, English-speaking AI-native Video Producer with experience in producing and editing video ads for performance marketing campaigns to join our team full-time (in San Francisco or Berlin on-site, hybrid or remote). In this role, you will work with our self-developed AI video engine to produce, edit and deliver video ads for the paid social campaigns of our clients. Your videos will reach millions of people across Meta, Google, LinkedIn and TikTok.

Why Join

  • Uplane is the best place to learn how to produce video ads with AI. This is the skill every creative lead will need. Learn how to do it today, not in three years.

  • AI does the grunt work, you do the creative work. Our engine handles the tedious stuff so your time goes into concept, storytelling and taste.

  • Millions of people will watch your videos.

  • Take ownership and grow quickly.

  • Join a fast-growing, VC-backed company.

  • Culture: fast-moving, ambitious, fun, humble.

Responsibilities

  • AI Video Ad Production: You use our powerful, self-developed AI video engine to produce, edit and design strong video ads that will be seen by millions of people. You are in charge, the AI helps you get there.

  • Team Collaboration: Work with an ambitious team of marketing managers and creative designers to ensure projects are executed to a high standard and in a timely manner.

  • Shape the AI engine: Give feedback to our product and engineering team and shape how our video engine will evolve and improve over time.

Requirements

  • Passion for video, you love scripting, editing, motion and creative work

  • Years of experience in producing / editing videos

  • Work experience in paid social or with performance marketing campaigns

  • Fast learner, hard-working, and stress-resistant

  • Curious and excited about AI rather than afraid of it

  • Fluent English

Nice to Have

  • You have won awards for your creative work

title: Network Developer
description: Senior Network Developer About Share Share is the global marketplace for bandwidth. We aggregate telco infrastructure across Africa (fiber routes, subsea capacity, data centers, cloud on-ramps) into a single intelligence layer. That lets ISPs, hyperscalers and AI companies get connectivity where they need it in seconds, not months. Today, bandwidth is bought and sold through slow, private, one-off deals, with almost no price transparency. We're replacing that with one neutral exchange: an API on top of real infrastructure, with prices set by actual supply and demand. It's already live across East Africa, with thousands of kilometers of fiber, 12 infrastructure providers, 10 data centers, and around 8 million people served. The Role Our network is the foundation of the product. Every route a customer provisions through our API has to exist, perform and stay up on real hardware. We're hiring a Senior Network Developer to design and build that network as software: a distributed, multi-provider fabric that engineers change through code, not by logging into devices. You'll own the network architecture end to end. That covers our BGP edge (transit, peering at KIXP and LINX, private interconnects with hyperscalers), the backbone, and the PoPs and data centers we're adding across the continent. You'll set the standards our network is built to, which partner ISPs connecting to us will inherit. As we grow, you'll also help build the network engineering team. What you'll do Design the backbone and PoP architecture as standard, repeatable building blocks, from edge to data center, so we can add capacity and new markets without redesigning each time. Drive our move to Segment Routing and a clean IP architecture, including IPv4 reuse, IPv6, and how customer and internal address space coexist. Build on disaggregated white-box hardware (Edgecore with IP Infusion OcNOS today), and make the hardware and software calls that keep us fast and affordable. Turn operations into software. That means a source of truth (Nautobot), templated config (Jinja), and CI/CD with validation, staged rollouts and rollback for every change. Build the telemetry and observability that show what the network is really doing. Use AI where it actually helps: anomaly detection, automated triage, and auto-remediation with a human in the loop. Own availability. Limit how much any failure can affect, mitigate first and diagnose second, and turn post-mortems into fixes in the system. Work with our software team on the API and provisioning layer that exposes the network to customers, and with partner ISPs' engineers on the hand-off. Help hire and develop the engineers who'll run this with you. Our Ideal Candidate 8+ years building and operating large networks at a hyperscaler, CDN, internet exchange, carrier or ISP. Deep BGP at scale: route policy, communities, RPKI, traffic engineering, peering and transit. Strong data center and backbone design. You know Clos/EVPN-VXLAN fabrics and MPLS or Segment Routing, and when each makes sense. Hands-on with white-box or disaggregated networking, including choosing hardware and knowing where the silicon limits you. You treat the network as code. You write automation yourself (Python or similar), and you've built or run the pipelines, source of truth and telemetry that make that safe. You've owned availability for something that couldn't go down, and can walk us through a real incident: what broke, how you found it, and what you changed. AI-native in how you work. You've built with these tools, not just used them, and you have a view on where they help in operations and where they don't. You think like an owner. You bring ideas, not tickets, and you want to help build a team, not just a network. A clear, direct communicator who's comfortable with partners' engineers and with our founders. Nice to have Experience at an internet exchange, or running peering at scale. Open networking stacks like SONiC, OcNOS or FRR, or contributions to them. Streaming telemetry (gNMI/gRPC, sFlow), and building your own monitoring tooling. 400G/800G and optical (ZR) deployments, including vendor selection and certification. Access networks (GPON/XGS-PON) and MikroTik or Huawei gear, since many partner ISPs run it. Building networks in emerging markets such as Africa or Latin America. DDoS mitigation at the edge. If you don't tick every box but have built and run large networks in production, apply anyway. title: Network Operation Engineer
description: Network Operations Engineer 1. About the role Share is the global marketplace for bandwidth. We aggregate telco infrastructure into a single layer and give ISPs, hyperscalers, and AI companies a clean path to deliver connectivity into every home and business across Kenya and the continent. Behind that marketplace is a real network: a BGP edge peering with Tier 1 transit, hyperscalers, and local exchanges, an MPLS backbone, aggregation and access gear, and the systems that watch all of it. For the partners who run on us, the network is the product, and the NOC is where they feel it. A clean shift is a partner who never knew anything happened. That is the bar. We are early and the team is small, so we cannot afford a pair of hands that only knows how to escalate. We need a capable network engineer who can stand a shift, resolve real faults without waking anyone, and then keep building the network while East Africa sleeps: propagation and peering checks, health passes across the estate, config changes through to merge, tickets off the board, automation that takes the next repetitive job off everyone's plate. The watching is the floor of this role, not the ceiling. The NOC you would be joining is not a legacy one. We are building it as an AI assisted operations environment from the ground up. The forwarding plane runs on open source routing and forwarding software, every device configuration lives in Git, and an LLM layer sits on top of the live network state. When something moves, that layer reads the telemetry, correlates it against the topology and the config history, and puts a probable cause and a candidate fix in front of the engineer on shift. The point is not to replace your judgment. It is to collapse the time between an alert firing and you knowing where to look, so mean time to repair is measured in minutes. You sit inside that system. You use it, you push back on it when it is wrong, and what you catch that it misses is part of how it gets smarter. As we build automation out across the NOC, you are not just a consumer of the tooling. You help write it. 2. What you'll do Watch, and know what you're looking at. Sit on our monitoring stack (Zabbix and Grafana dashboards, flow telemetry, alerting) and actually read it. Learn what normal looks like so abnormal jumps out at you: a BGP session that dropped, a link that went down, latency climbing on a path, a capacity threshold breached, a partner suddenly pushing or pulling nothing. Troubleshoot and resolve. This is where you earn your seat. Confirm the alert is real, gather the facts, and localise the fault: one peer or many, us or upstream, a real outage or a monitoring blip. The assistive layer surfaces a likely diagnosis and a suggested fix, the config history is right there in Git, and the runbooks are live. Your job is to read all of it critically, decide what is actually true, and close out what you can on your own. Every ticket you resolve yourself is one our senior people did not get pulled out of deep work, or out of bed, to deal with. Keep the network healthy, not just alive. A quiet shift is not an idle one. Run the proactive passes: check that routes are propagating the way they should, that RPKI and filter chains are doing their job, that peering and transit sessions are clean across the edge, that no PoP is drifting toward a capacity wall. Catch the slow degradations that never trip an alert. The day team should inherit a network in a known good state. Build and automate. The repetitive parts of this job should not stay repetitive. Write the scripts that turn a manual check into a scheduled one. Push our config automation forward (Jinja driven generation, NAPALM or NETCONF/gNMI against the devices) so changes ship from data, not from memory. When the assistive layer keeps missing the same thing, that is a candidate for automation, and you are well placed to build it during the hours nobody else is online. Move the work forward. You are part of the network team, working the same board they do. Pick up tickets from the Linear queue, take config changes through review to merge, and keep our source of truth (Nautobot) accurate as the estate changes. Real work lands while East Africa is offline, so the team wakes up further ahead than they went to bed. Report exactly what is happening. For everything you cannot or should not fix alone, the handoff has to be clean: what is wrong, where, since when, what is affected, whether it is getting worse, and what you have already tried. No guessing dressed up as fact. No "the internet is down." A clear, written incident note a senior engineer can act on the moment they open it, and a tidy handover to the East Africa team at the end of your shift. Escalate well. Know the ladder cold: what you are cleared to touch, what you must not touch alone, and who to bring in for what. Escalating early on a genuine outage is good judgment. Sitting silently on a problem because you were unsure is the one thing that gets people out of bed angry. Handle what you can, raise the rest fast and clearly, and do not turn either dial too far. 3. Who we're looking for A network engineer who can stand on their own through a shift, and who treats the quiet hours as time to build rather than time to wait. You will not be the most senior engineer on this team, and you do not need to be. The people you escalate to are CCIE level. What we need from you is independence and range: work a problem properly, resolve a fair share of it yourself, and use what is left of the shift to actually move the network forward. Pair that with clear reporting, sound judgment about when to bring in help, and the instinct to question a machine's suggestion rather than follow it blindly, and you are who we are looking for. Must-have Strong networking competence, held in your hands rather than on paper. CCNA and well beyond it. You understand TCP/IP, routing and switching, IP addressing and subnetting, DNS, DHCP, NAT, and how they behave when they go wrong. Real troubleshooting instinct. Given a degraded link or a dropped session, you know where to look and what to rule out. You can read BGP session state, follow a path with ping and traceroute, and tell a local fault from an upstream one without waiting to be told. Working BGP knowledge. Reading communities and route policy, spotting a flap or a leaky origin, understanding how transit, peering, and RPKI behave at the edge. Comfortable on the gear and the CLI. Linux, network device CLIs, and dashboards are familiar ground. We run MikroTik (RouterOS) across the network and so do many partners, so RouterOS experience is a real plus. Comfortable working with config in Git. Configuration lives in repos, not on devices. Reading a diff, understanding why a config changed, and proposing one yourself should not be foreign to you. Some scripting, and the appetite to do more. Bash or Python, enough to automate the repetitive parts away and to grow into our config and automation pipelines. We are not hiring a button pusher. Clear written English. You can describe a technical situation accurately and briefly so someone picking it up cold understands it instantly. Calm under pressure and dependable. When the graphs go red you get more precise, not more panicked. You show up for every shift, alert and on time. Located in New Zealand or a nearby time zone where covering our deep overnight maps onto your normal working day. Nice-to-have CCNP, or MikroTik MTCNA / MTCRE. Prior NOC, ISP, or carrier operations experience. Hands on with MPLS (L3VPN, EVPN) and the multi-tenant isolation a shared backbone needs. Exposure to open source and white box routing or forwarding stacks (SONiC, IP Infusion OcNOS, FRR, or similar). Network source of truth and automation tooling (Nautobot, NAPALM, Jinja config generation, NETCONF or gNMI). Familiarity with a monitoring stack such as Zabbix, Grafana, Loki, or Prometheus, and with flow telemetry. Working familiarity with FreeRADIUS, CoA and Disconnect flows, and how session control and accounting hook into the network. Exposure to applying ML or AI in network operations: anomaly detection, predictive failure analysis, automated triage or remediation. IPv6 and dual stack exposure, and internet exchange operations (looking glass and route server behaviour, IRR and RPKI hygiene). 4. What we offer A seat inside a serious, very senior network team , with people who have deep service provider backgrounds and will sharpen you fast. You will see how a real carrier network behaves under live conditions. A front row seat to how a network actually gets run in 2026. Open source forwarding, config as code, and an LLM layer doing real operational work. Not a slide about the future of network operations, but the environment you would work in every shift, and help build. Real engineering, not just monitoring. The role is built so the quiet hours go into automation, propagation and health work, and tickets off the board. The path into deeper network engineering and automation work is the plan, not a vague someday. Competitive salary and private health and wellness benefits , fully remote, in a mission driven, investor backed company building the backbone of Africa's next generation internet. A network engineer who can stand on their own through a shift, and who treats the quiet hours as time to build rather than time to wait. You will not be the most senior engineer on this team, and you do not need to be. The people you escalate to are CCIE level. title: Backend Software Engineer - Indexing

Every firm can license the same AI models, but no two firms share the same institutional knowledge. Decades of experience, work product, and precedent are often trapped across systems, underused and inaccessible. DeepJudge makes this expertise instantly available through world-class enterprise search and AI infrastructure, enabling firms to automate workflows, build knowledge-powered applications, and turn experience into a lasting advantage. Our technology is trusted by many of the world’s leading law firms, including Freshfields, Gunderson Dettmer, Holland & Knight, Arent Fox, and Cozen O’Connor. Headquartered in Switzerland with a growing team across North America, we are expanding rapidly and shaping the future of how professional knowledge is discovered and applied. At DeepJudge, we move fast, think rigorously, and care deeply about what we build. We combine cutting-edge research with close collaboration with our clients to deliver solutions that truly make an impact. If you want to be part of a team defining how AI transforms high-stakes knowledge work, this is the place to do it. About the Role: We’re looking for a Backend Software Engineer to join our team and take meaningful ownership from day one. You’ll work closely with smart, driven, and genuinely fun people who are passionate about tackling the complex challenges involved in building a high-performance product at scale. Our indexing system is the backbone of our search engine, processing queries over hundreds of millions of documents in fractions of a second. Building and maintaining these indices within tight time and resource constraints requires highly performant, scalable software. To achieve this, we rely on modern technologies in distributed and parallel computing, database systems, and cloud platforms. You’ll leverage the strengths of these technologies to meet demanding throughput and latency requirements. Your responsibilities will include: Design, develop, and maintain efficient, scalable backend services using modern tools and frameworks Take ownership of core components of our indexing infrastructure Collaborate with other engineers to define, design, and ship new features Optimize performance and scalability across our data processing pipelines Integrate with third-party data providers and effectively use their APIs Review code and contribute to a high standard of code quality and maintainability Participate in agile development processes, including sprint planning, daily stand-ups, and retrospectives You're a great fit if you: Have a Master’s degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience Have 2+ years of experience as a Backend Software Engineer, ideally in a scale-up or fast-growing environment Have strong experience with concurrent and parallel programming and understand how to write correct, efficient code under load Are highly proficient in Python, our primary backend language. title: Software Engineer, Robot Autonomy (Planning & Navigation)
description: Our Mission At Laelaps AI, we believe robotics is entering a transformative decade, much like the arrival of the internet. Advances in AI, cloud computing, and hardware are reshaping what autonomous systems can do. Our mission is to build the intelligent software that powers physical security in the real world - enabling robots and sensors to handle dangerous and critical tasks that humans shouldn't have to. By engineering the orchestration layer for intelligent security, we aim to create a world that is safer, more secure, and more resilient. We're a strong founding team based in Zurich, backed by visionary investors and advisors. We are engineering the future of security today! THE ROLE As a Software Engineer on Robot Autonomy, you will make our robots navigate dependably across real customer sites. Our stack works. The gap between working and dependable is the whole job. Every new site tests how a robot understands its surroundings and chooses where to go: a ramp the planner avoids, a narrow passage that exposes a poor route, a gate that changes the map, a person who steps into the robot's path, or localization drift that builds over a long patrol. You treat those cases as the real navigation problem to solve, not as edge cases. You'll shape the technical choices behind reliable navigation, from sensor selection, ground segmentation, and traversability estimation to predicting how people and vehicles move and planning safe, efficient routes around them. The system has to work day and night, in challenging weather, across different embodiments and changing site conditions. We measure success by whether the robot completes its patrol on a live site, not by how it performs in simulation. WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON Navigation and path-planning design: how robots represent traversable space, select routes, avoid obstacles, and reach goals across complex sites. Sensor integration driven by navigation requirements, including what ground segmentation and traversability estimation need in day, night, and challenging weather. Environment understanding: how the robot distinguishes ground from obstacles and estimates which terrain is safe and practical to traverse. Behavior prediction: anticipate how people, vehicles, and other dynamic obstacles will move, and plan routes that stay safe and efficient around them. Field reliability: reproduce failures from deployments, find the root cause, and fix it at the right layer, from sensor data and maps to costmaps, planners, and recovery behaviors. Planning under imperfect localization: plans that stay useful when the state estimate drifts and the robot must execute routes in tight or dynamic environments, working with the rest of Robot Autonomy on localization and control. Validation on real robots: logs, simulation, and repeatable field tests to verify that design choices and changes hold across routes, lighting, weather, and site layouts. New autonomy capabilities: work with the engineers building the operator application and backend so operator requests and new robot capabilities rest on a sound navigation design. The field feedback loop: work closely with forward-deployed engineers to turn site issues into bugs, design changes, and improvements to the navigation stack. Regular site visits to build a practical understanding of how robots and sensors behave in real operating conditions. WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR We're looking for an engineer who has taken a robotics system from unreliable to dependable and takes ownership beyond individual tickets. You can explain why you made a navigation design choice and what it costs. When a robot takes a bad route, you can tell whether the planner, the map, the state estimate, or the robot's behavior is at fault, and you fix the right one. You are comfortable in the field and want to understand how robots behave in real customer environments. YOUR BACKGROUND: A Master's degree or PhD in mechanical engineering, computer science, robotics, electrical engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Proven track record building and deploying navigation on ground mobile robots in the real world (3+ years or equivalent depth). Hands-on experience with mobile robot navigation and path planning: route or local planning, static and dynamic obstacle avoidance, costmaps, or recovery behaviors. Understanding of how mapping and localization affect navigation, and the ability to diagnose when a planning issue is actually caused by the map, the state estimate, or robot behavior. Understanding of how lighting, weather, terrain, and sensor limitations affect perception and navigation, with experience developing or validating systems for demanding real-world conditions. Hands-on experience with robotics sensors and hardware, especially LiDAR, IMUs, and cameras. You can investigate issues across software, networking, and hardware boundaries. Experience testing and debugging navigation on physical robots using logs, visualization, simulation, and repeatable field tests. Strong ROS 2, C++, and Python skills. Clear communication of navigation and path-planning design choices and their trade-offs. Willingness to visit customer sites regularly. NICE TO HAVE: Experience with legged robots or with more than one robot embodiment. Experience with Nav2 or a comparable navigation framework. Motion prediction or planning among people and vehicles, such as trajectory forecasting or socially aware navigation. Terrain mapping and traversability methods: elevation mapping, learned traversability, or semantic segmentation for navigation. Experience with night-time or all-weather sensing, such as thermal cameras or LiDAR in rain and fog. Background in security, defence, or other safety-critical robotics deployments. What We Offer Ownership: you are able to ship products and deliver project end-to-end. Mission: autonomous security that keeps people and critical sites safe, including in defence. Career path: a ground-floor seat with real runway. Prove your value and you will not have barriers to grow. Team: work directly with PhD-level co-founders in AI, Robotics, and Physics, alongside a strong (and fun) founding team. Compensation: Competitive equity/salary package Culture: International founding team that is serious about building but does not take itself too seriously. Find Jobs in Switzerland on Arbeitnow

The role: You take a business-first, data-driven view of what's holding a client's growth back, use AI to diagnose it faster and deeper than a traditional audit, and turn it into a concrete plan that works. Key & Essential Skills: Ideally 7+ years in a performance agency (not media buying), including 3+ years leading a team of 3+. Deep knowledge of at least 3 marketing channels (e.g. SEO, Google Ads, Meta, content), with CHF 1M+ in total managed budget. Comfortable using AI as a core tool for analysis, reporting and consulting. What makes you a fit: You like taking ownership and seeing things through. You give honest feedback, to clients and to us. You know when to plan carefully, when to perfect, and when to move fast. You think like an entrepreneur: curious, commercially minded, always moving forward. Perks: Beautiful office in Seefeld, Zurich. You'll have real responsibility and influence - and a team that has your back. If you see something that could be improved, speak up - we're listening. description: Camunda is the enterprise platform for agentic orchestration , enabling organizations to coordinate AI agents, people, and systems across complex, end-to-end business processes. With built-in governance, auditability, and human oversight, Camunda gives enterprises the control they need to move AI from pilots to production — safely and at scale. Trusted by over 700 organizations worldwide , including 9 of top 10 US banks, Camunda helps enterprises boost operational efficiency, accelerate time-to-value, and deliver better customer experiences. Fully remote and global, we are in the middle of something bigger: transforming into an AI-first organisation, built on our own platform . We use Agentic AI to automate, orchestrate intelligent processes, and elevate human contribution across every team. Named GP Bullhound’s Top 100 Next Unicorn list, 2025 Great Place to Work certified. Visionary in 2025 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Business Orchestration and Automation Technologies. ranked 3rd in Flexa's 2026 Most Flexible Companies , We’re growing fast and looking for top talent to join our team. If you want meaningful work, visible impact and put something genuinely rare on your CV, keep reading. About the role: We're hiring a Senior Software Engineer, Quality to build the agentic layer of how Camunda tests its software. We treat quality as an engineering discipline. We build test infrastructure the way we build our product — real design decisions, real trade-offs, real ownership. What's changing is how that work gets done: we're moving from hand-written test suites toward agents that design, generate, maintain and triage tests across the lifecycle. We need someone to build both the agents and the infrastructure that makes them dependable, and to help shape our Quality AI strategy. You'll support product teams that ship features without dedicated QA. Your job is not to become their testing safety net. It's to build the tooling and practices that let builders own quality themselves — and to stay close enough to real features to know where that tooling breaks. Camunda also ships AI capabilities in its own product, so the evaluation practice you build for agent-driven testing feeds directly into how we test non-deterministic features. You'll join colleagues who live our FAITH values: Focus, Ambition, Integrity, Talent and Humor. Curious about the kind of challenges you'll work on at Camunda? Watch this quick 30-minute talk from our engineers to learn more about the new Camunda Exporter and how we’re solving complex problems at scale What You’ll Be Doing: Build and operate agents across the testing lifecycle — test design, generation, maintenance, execution and failure triage. Own the infrastructure that makes agent-driven testing reliable: environments, test data, tool interfaces, guardrails, runtime and cost control. Define how we measure agent output quality, so teams can trust results instead of hand-reviewing them. Apply that evaluation practice to testing Camunda 8's own AI capabilities. Work hands-on with new features as teams build them, enough to keep the tooling honest. Raise the quality capability of teams — patterns, tooling, enablement. Success is what builders can do themselves, not the number of tests you wrote. What You Bring: Ability and/or willingness to use our product 5+ years as a software engineer. You write production code daily and would be credible on a product team; quality is your domain, not a step down from development. Production experience building test infrastructure, developer tooling or internal platforms that other engineers depend on — designed and owned, not just extended. Hands-on work with LLMs or agent frameworks: prompt and context design, tool use, handling non-determinism, and evaluating output quality. This is the differentiator for the role. Comfort with distributed systems and CI at scale. Camunda 8 is a process orchestration platform; testing it means reasoning about concurrency, state and timing. The ability to drive adoption in teams that don't report to you. You've built something another team chose to use, and you know what to do when the first version isn't picked up. Nice-to-haves: Experience evaluating or benchmarking LLM systems. Open-source contribution experience. Java, TypeScript or Python; Kubernetes and Helm. Background in developer tooling or platform engineering. This role is an existing vacancy #LI-AG1 #LI-Remote #USEAST What We Have to Offer: Compensation We offer competitive, fair, and transparent compensation. Salary ranges are location-based, with Standard and Major markets (global tech hubs) reflecting local competition. The Annual Total Target Cash (base salary + 100% variable target, where applicable) shown below spans from the minimum in a Standard market to the maximum in a Major market. Final offers depend on skills , experience , and location , and we typically hire in the first half of the range to allow room for growth: United States: $143,800.00 to $231,900.00 United Kingdom: £90,300.00 to £148,500.00 Singapore: S$178,600.00 to S$267,900.00 Canada: C$152,700.00 to C$251,200.00 If you’re based elsewhere, you’ll be hired via Remote.com (our global employer partner), and your Talent Acquisition Partner will provide a personalized Total Rewards Calculator after your first interview. Equity: We also offer equity (where applicable) through our Virtual Stock Option Plan (VSOP) . Benefits & Perks We invest in your wellbeing, growth, and ability to connect, along with perks that support you no matter where you’re based. Our benefits are globally designed and locally delivered where applicable. Remote & Flexible: Work from anywhere with the setup that suits you, home office budget, co-working space support, and flexible time off to recharge when you need it. In Person Connection: We invest in meaningful face time through our Annual Kickoff (Vienna in 2025, Madrid in 2026!), team offsites, and Camundi Connection Budgets , including contributing to meetups while travelling,, and local gatherings with fellow Camundi. Health & Wellbeing: Access locally tailored healthcare, Modern Health for global mental wellbeing, and our Live Well Lifestyle Spending Account (LSA), a flexible, global benefit that puts you in control of your whole life, not just work, from: staying active, to caring for family, exploring personal passions, meaningful experiences, and investing in your financial wellbeing. The Live Well program launches in 2026 and scales to €1,000 annually from 2027 . Financial Security: Retirement and pension plans (often with company contributions), plus life and disability insurance where relevant. concretely to their commercial shape, trade-offs and delivery.</li> <li>You have grown a practice, capability or go-to-market asset, for example a reusable accelerator taken to market, combining client and delivery teams, while leading primarily on strategy and advisory.</li> <li>You bring significant hands-on and leadership experience in data and AI (typically 10+ years) and, above all, the appetite to keep building: growing accounts, teams and capability rather than only overseeing them.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Professional Skills</strong></p> <ul> <li>You understand the importance of
